met_analysis:
The Well-Marked Low Pressure Area over southeast Rajasthan & neighbourhood persisted over the same region at 0830 hrs IST of today, the 01st August, 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation extends upto 7.6 km above mean sea level tilting southwestwards with height. It is very likely to move west-northwestwards across South Rajasthan and weaken further into a Low Pressure Area during next 24 hours.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now pass through Jaisalmer, centre of Well-Marked Low Pressureoversoutheast Rajasthan and neighbourhood, Sidhi, Dehri, Malda, thence eastwards towards Manipur.
A trough runs form southwest Rajasthan to northeast Bihar across centre of Well-Marked Low Pressureoversoutheast Rajasthan and neighbourhood, across northern parts of Madhya Pradesh, southeast Uttar Pradesh and extends upto 4.5 km above mean sea level tilting southwestwards with height.
The offshore trough at mean sea level now runs from South Gujarat to Kerala.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northeast Assam & neighbourhood extending upto 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over southeast Himachal Pradesh & neighbourhood at 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over Himachal Pradesh & neighbourhood at 5.8 km above mean sea level persists.
An east-west shear zone runs roughly along latitude 22°N across central & adjoining north peninsular India between 3.1 & 5.8 km above mean sea level tilting southwards with height has become less marked.
